evidence.schema_paragraph_host: `mem_source` records *where the supervisor read its memory facts*, because the 60 GB allowance is about the host that holds the workload — the 121 GB GB10 / GX10 unified pool — not necessarily the machine the CLI runs on. Two sources exist: `"local"` (`LocalMeminfo`, reading `/proc/meminfo` here, `SPCC_MEMINFO_PATH` overrides the path in tests) and `"ssh:<host>"` (`RemoteMeminfo`, running `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> cat /proc/meminfo`, read-only). A remote read that fails raises and is refused; it never becomes zero. `--target-host` (or `SPCC_TARGET_HOST`) selects the source at `open-window`; `run` reuses the source recorded in the window unless it is given its own `--target-host`.
evidence.schema_paragraph_enforcement: `enforcement` states what the window can actually prove. `"cgroup"` is claimed **only** when `mem_source` is `"local"`: the cgroup written by `run` (`spcc-<job>-<pid>`, `memory.max = 60 GiB`) governs the child this supervisor spawned, so `memory.peak` is a real measurement of that child. A remote host can only ever yield **`"declared-only"`**: the supervisor cannot write a cgroup on another machine, so there is no measured peak and no kernel-enforced cap — only the declared peak admitted at open time plus the sampled `MemAvailable`. Do not fake a cgroup for a remote window; the mode is recorded precisely so a reader can tell the two apart.
evidence.remote_note: The ssh path was NOT exercised: no network in this unit. Remote behaviour is proven through injected readers (`RemoteMeminfo(host, runner=...)`); the default runner is a BatchMode ssh cat whose non-zero exit, empty output, timeout, or unparseable text raises. Tests assert no local cgroup is created for remote windows.

next_unit_hint: When a real GX10 is reachable, open a window with --target-host <gx10> to exercise RemoteMeminfo end to end; it must record enforcement declared-only and can never return VERIFIED. If remote enforcement is ever required, it needs a supervisor process running on the GX10 itself (cgroup lives there), not a local one.
